The Preply English-Tutor Market

Comprehensive market analysis & tutor case study
8,952 unique tutors · 161 countries · 8 site locales · collected 1–2 September 2026 from public listing pages · prices in USD per 50-minute lesson
Executive summary. Where a tutor is from is the price system: country explains 41% of price variance, the “native speaker” flag alone explains none. “Native” spans two unrelated markets ($25 median for US/UK/CA/AU/IE/NZ natives vs $10 for natives from other countries). The platform median is $17 — but Preply’s promoted storefront shows a $38 slate. Ratings are saturated at 4.9+; review count is the real reputation currency. Higher-priced tutors keep students ~2.3× longer than lower-priced ones. And the case-study tutor — an example profile at $20/lesson — is charging newcomer prices on a top-16% track record, roughly $12k/year below the peer benchmark.

1 · How the data was collected

A Playwright scraper collected tutor listing-card data (never robots.txt-disallowed profile pages), rate-limited to one page per ~2–5s. The English site's ranking window pins at ~6.4k visible tutors (pagination returns HTTP 403 past page 99; re-crawls in fresh sessions add ~0 new). The breakthrough: Preply's other language locales (/it/ /es/ /pt/ /fr/ /de/ /pl/ /tr/) cache their rankings separately — crawling them (URLs from Preply's own sitemaps, card text parsed with a per-locale vocabulary table, country normalized from flag ISO codes) added ~2,500 tutors the English pages never served. Dedicated native-speaker listings were probed to depth and were ~95% already covered, so the native segment (5,159 tutors) is effectively a census of what Preply lists.

“Native speaker” is two different markets: US/UK natives ($24–25) and Cameroonian natives ($5) share a checkbox, not a market. Cameroon is the third-largest native-tutor country on the platform (586 tutors) — ahead of Canada and Australia. Within the same country, natives carry a modest real premium: $19 vs $15 (~+25%).

3 · Price landscape & reputation dynamics

  • Median $17; decile spread $6 → $35. 21% of tutors charge under $10; only 21 tutors touch $100.
  • 48% of prices are multiples of $5 — $10/$15/$20/$25 are the shelves of the market (pink spikes above).
  • Newcomers price like newcomers: the 1,403 tutors with zero reviews enter at $12 median vs $18 established; US-native newcomers enter at $15 vs $25 — a 40% discount. “Start low, climb with reviews” is the de facto market convention.
  • Ratings are dead as a signal — 88% of rated tutors show ≥4.9 stars. Review count is what ladders price: $15 (1–10 reviews) → $20 (11–50) → $25 (200+). Among US natives: $20 → $26.5 → $30.
  • Reviews↔price correlation is real but modest and front-loaded: Spearman ρ = 0.18 overall (Pearson 0.11), rising to ρ = 0.26 within US natives — country differences mute the global number. Median price climbs $13 → $20 across the first ~20 reviews, then the market-wide curve plateaus; beyond that, reviews keep paying only inside premium segments.
  • Experience is a power law: median 564 lifetime lessons, p99 = 10,038, max 22,694 (~19,000 hours).
  • Lifetime gross proxy (price × lessons): ≈ $270M across the sample; median tutor ≈ $9,200 lifetime. By country: US $56M, UK $55M, then Ukraine $22M.
  • Preply’s commission (verified): 100% of every trial lesson, plus a sliding cut on regular lessons by cumulative hours — 33% (0–20h) → 28% (21–50h) → 25% (51–200h) → 22% (201–400h) → 18% floor (400+h). Take-home is 67–82% of the figures above. The structure squeezes newcomers twice: the highest rate lands on the lowest prices ($12 median) while trials are free — an entering tutor can net under $8/lesson.

4 · Full-dataset EDA

5 · Case study: pricing a top-16% tutor at $20

Profile (an example tutor drawn from the dataset): US native English speaker, also a native Spanish speaker, certified medical interpreter. On Preply: 5.0★, 23 reviews, 2,809 lessons (~110/month), business/career focus, $20 per 50-minute lesson.

Benchmarks (vs 1,269 US native tutors)

  • 2,809 lessons place this tutor in the top 16–17% by teaching volume — yet $20 is what US natives with under ten reviews charge, and sits below 58% of US natives.
  • The closest peer cell — US natives with 2,000–4,500 lessons (n=192) — charges median $29 (p75 $40). Matching them ≈ +$11,880/year at this pace.
  • Result is robust: widening to all 2,942 Western natives moves each rung by at most $1.

The one gap: review conversion (19th percentile)

The tutor banks 8.2 reviews per 1,000 lessons vs the experienced-tutor median of 13 — slower than 81% of comparable tutors. Reviews gate the $26.5 → $30 rungs, and 2,809 lessons of goodwill is an unusually large unharvested reserve.

Why a raise is low-risk (from the market data)

  • Retention rises with price: the $20–35 band keeps students 98 lessons vs 74 in $10–20.
  • A low price doesn’t buy visibility: promoted tutors have a median price of $38, and 98% have 11+ reviews (the example tutor qualifies with 23). Staying at $20 earns nothing algorithmically.
  • The badge that pays: US natives with Super Tutor sit at $28.50 vs $22 without. The “Professional” credential badge carries no premium anywhere in the data.

Recommendations

  • Now: lead the profile headline with the two rare facts — US native English + native Spanish; certified medical interpreter — and claim the “English for Spanish speakers” and medical-English discovery pages. Ask for a review at every milestone lesson.
  • Next new student: $25 (existing students keep their rate).
  • At ~50 reviews: reprice toward $29–30; pursue Super Tutor criteria in the dashboard.
  • Trajectory: $26,400/yr today → ≈$38,000/yr at peer pricing, zero extra teaching hours.

6 · What this means for learners

The storefront-vs-inventory gap works in reverse as shopping advice — the default “top picks” slate is $38 median in a $17 market:

  • Paginate or filter past page 1 — the same 4.9-star, heavily-reviewed tutors exist at half the promoted price.
  • Ignore the star rating (everyone shows 4.9+); compare review counts and lessons taught.
  • “Native speaker” alone tells you nothing — the badge spans $5 Cameroonian tutors and $80 US coaches. Decide what you need (accent model, exam prep, conversation volume) and filter for that.
  • The value corner: experienced non-Western natives and premium non-natives (Ukraine, South Africa) — 800+ lifetime lessons at $7–20.
  • The “Professional” badge is decoration; Super Tutor actually correlates with retention.

7 · Limitations

  • Listing-card data only; profile pages are robots.txt-disallowed and were never visited.
  • Single snapshot (Sept 2026); no arrival or repricing dynamics.
  • students appears to count active students vs lifetime lessons, so lessons-per-student overstates absolute retention (comparisons remain valid).
  • Coverage is the union of 8 locale ranking windows (~8,952 of a claimed ~46k), not a uniform random sample. Native tutors are near-exhaustively covered; long-tail non-natives are under-sampled.
  • Reputation-price relationships are correlational; tutors who survive to high review counts may charge more because they are good, not because reviews permit it.
